title: Overflow Retry and Exact Accumulation-Group Preservation

policy.objective: Preserve every accumulation group and the planned number of successful optimizer updates when GradScaler detects overflow.
before_each_group: Record the current epoch and next microbatch position.
Snapshot all available PyTorch CUDA RNG states.
normal_attempt: Process the same accumulation group in its defined order.
Divide each microbatch loss by the actual group size.
If gradients are finite, clip gradients to max_norm 1.0.
Record the GradScaler scale before optimizer stepping.
Compare the new scale with the previous scale.
successful_update: Treat the attempt as successful when the GradScaler scale does not decrease.
Advance the training position beyond the completed group.
Clear gradients before the next group.
overflow_retry: Treat a decreased GradScaler scale as a skipped optimizer update.
Restore the exact pre-group Python, NumPy, PyTorch CPU, and CUDA RNG states.
Retry the identical accumulation group with the reduced scale.
Do not advance the epoch or microbatch position until success.

retry_limit.on_limit: Abort safely with an explicit error and preserve the last verified recovery checkpoint. Never silently discard the group.

policy.partial_group: The final group of six examples follows the same retry policy. Its loss normalization remains division by six.
policy.checkpointing: Do not create a normal progress checkpoint between an overflow skip and its immediate retry. If execution is interrupted, resume from the last successful checkpoint and replay work as required.

implementation_notes: The GradScaler scale comparison is used to detect overflow skips: a decreased scale indicates a skipped optimizer update.
A successful update may leave the scale unchanged or increase it.
RNG restoration reproduces the stochastic random-state inputs for the retry; it does not guarantee bitwise-identical CUDA execution when nondeterministic kernels are present.
The retry limit is an operational safety guard, not a model hyperparameter or a change to the research experiment.
